_note: EXTERIOR round 2, 2026-08-23. Room 3 'Backyard' is not a room: it is the back of the house, seen only from the whole-house level ('all'). SHOOT WITH --level all, NEVER --level 1, and with --sun-azimuth 335 or the rear elevation renders unlit. Build scripts: scratchpad/ext/ (kit.py shared helpers incl. deck_surface/railing/stair, the board + wicker PNG tiles and the new uv_box; b_deck.py, b_furn.py; probe.py pixel->world raycast, scan.py / hmap.py shell-terrain scanners, meas.py metering). The landscape is procedural in frontend/js/environment.js (addGroundCover + addBackYard); the deck and its furniture are placed objects so the owner can move them.

_deck._height_decision: COMMITTED, replacing round 1's 3.95/3.30 compromise. What the photographs fix is the deck's relationship to the HOUSE, not its height above the lawn: 'Backyard v3 9' and 'v3 2' both put the deck surface level with the rear door THRESHOLD - you walk straight out - and the 4 risers down to the grass exist because the real lot falls away behind the house. This shell does not model that fall; its rear grade (2.13) is FLUSH with its own ground floor. So 'photographed height above the lawn' and 'photographed height relative to the house' are mutually exclusive here - 4 risers up from the lawn would put the deck 2.7 ft above the interior floor and you would step UP into the house. Taken: the HOUSE relationship, which is visible from every view. Recovered where the shell allows: the east strip really is 2.24 ft lower, so the EAST flight gets its photographed four risers, and the lower deck was pushed east from x 24.5 to 27.5 past the grade break so a third of it genuinely floats on posts with a visible fascia. Result: rail top 5.72 (upper) / 5.40 (lower) instead of 7.00 / 6.35.
_deck._rail_over_the_door: Round 2's critic cited my_rear_elev.png showing the rail crossing the opening. 'Backyard v3 2' shows the REAL rail crossing the real patio doors' lower third from that same ground-level viewpoint, because the rail stands 18 ft in front of the wall. That overlap is projection, not collision, and it is what the photograph does. See r2_back_elev.png against 'Backyard v3 2.jpg'.
_deck.contact_shadows: baked into the deck surface as VERTEX-COLOUR darkening on a 0.8 ft grid, not as decal quads: a decal at deck height either z-fights or, if opaque, erases the board texture. Ramp exponent 1.15, radii run ~0.8 ft past each piece's footprint, eight pieces listed in b_deck.py SHADOWS.

_wicker.the_real_defect: Round 2's critic said the wicker has no weave. It did not, and the cause was STRUCTURAL, not a texture-strength problem: roomkit.glb's box() emits NO UVs, so every wicker panel sampled texel (0,0) forever and rendered as flat paint. kit.py now has uv_box()/add_uv_box() - a box with per-face planar UVs - and every wicker part uses it.
_wicker.tile: wicker_tex rewritten: 8 px cells (one over-under pair), warp and weft swapping which is on top per cell, a dark gap line between strands, base 250 against gap 138. Round 1's 242-against-196 on a 4 px cell was a 19% modulation; a real basketweave is nearer 45%.
_wicker.scale: WEAVE = 1.15 repeats per foot, about 1.3 inch per pair - the top of the real strand range, chosen so the weave survives the mipmap at the exterior fly-to distance rather than for closest fidelity in one close-up.
_wicker.colour: #bfbab1 (warm) -> #a4a3a7. The photographed wicker meters RGB 169,166,175 - B above R; round 1 rendered 195,193,187.

_environment_js.lawn: Shared with room 11 - see rooms/11.json _environment_js.lawn. Same disc, same tile, same world-space vertex tint.
_environment_js.beds: narrow river-rock borders at the foot of the treeline and one wider apron beside the deck's east steps, at 4.4 cobbles/sq ft (front yard runs 7.0). The rear border was moved from z -57.5..-52.5 to -53.6..-48.4 so it straddles the pad's rear edge, which is where 'Backyard v3 5' puts the mulch line - on the far edge of the lawn, not out beyond it.
_environment_js.specimen: addPhotinia() - NEW, replacing addMound(...,'red'). Round 1 built a 12 x 4 ft BURGUNDY PANCAKE at RGB 114,60,66 (R-G +54). v3 9 x 1000-1075 and v3 5 x 740-960 show a SPHERE about 9 ft each way whose body is olive-green (metered 93,90,64 and 95,99,75, R-G between -5 and +5) with red new growth only on the sunlit tips. Now authored green-dominant with the red as a minority of the upper vertices. Round 1's comment said it was 'sized and sited to also swallow the shell GLB's leftover parasol RIBS' - the ribs went with house.js SHELL_CUTS, so that job no longer exists and this is authored purely to the photograph.
_environment_js.mounds: addMound takes a `kind` (green/dark/olive/grey) and a per-mound squash, and a `sphere` flag. Round 1 gave every one of ~20 the same squash and hue, which read as twenty copies of one object.
_environment_js.weepers: addWeeper() - NEW. The layered/weeping specimens standing free on the lawn in v3 7 and along the boundary in v3 5. Two earlier passes rendered them as stacks of brown lily pads (y scale 0.30 then 0.62 with 1.55 s tier spacing at hue 0.09-0.15); the tiers overlap heavily now at y 0.66 / 0.95 s spacing and the hue is a bronze-green 0.195-0.245.
_environment_js.feeder: addFeeder() - the pole bird feeder at the boundary bed (v3 5 x 1140-1170)
_environment_js.treeline: TWO ranks across the rear at 4.5 ft spacing jittered in both axes, plus denser side lines and small flowering trees inside the line. This is the round-2 critic's headline back-yard gap: with the shell's rear fence cut, the yard ran flat green to a razor-straight horizon. A CAM KEEP-OUT guard now skips any big tree within 22 ft of either exterior fly-to camera ground point ((47.1, 97.2) front, (-18.5, -77.9) back) - a 33 ft shade tree has a ~12 ft crown and the denser rank put leaves over the lens.
_environment_js.understory: mounds at 2.6-5.6 ft spacing along all three boundaries, mixed kinds
_environment_js.neighbours: FIVE massings, not two: v3 7 shows three rooflines across the boundary and one hard left. addNeighbour rebuilt (see rooms/11.json) and moved into its own matte bucket.

_residual_shell_props._note: REPORT ONLY - house.js is not ours. These are what is left of the shell's terrace enclosure fence after SHELL_CUTS took its pickets and top rails. Each is a thin bar at y 0.654-0.765, about 0.6 ft proud of our lawn, and each renders as a thin WHITE LINE lying on the grass. Found with scratchpad/ext/probe.py (pixel -> world, visible-filtered) and measured with scan.py / hmap.py.
_residual_shell_props.safety: Neither box contains terrain that must stay: the ground there is at 0.16 (below y0 0.45) and the raised pad at 2.13 (above y1 1.05). They do clip the legs of the terrace lounge props, which environment.js hideShellPatioProps already hides.

_open: The rear elevation still renders a flat desaturated grey even at --sun-azimuth 335: one directional sun, no bounce. Not charged to this yard. Separately, the shell's siding is authored warm off-white (189,184,180, R>B) where the house is cool blue-grey in every photograph (148,164,181, B>G>R) - shell material, not ours.
The four terrace-fence footing runs above still render as white lines on the lawn. Boxes supplied; house.js is not ours to edit.

check_pick only takes an integer level, so it cannot be run against these two outdoor rooms at all - and even at --level 1 it would sample the room slab at world y 8, above every piece here. It is not evidence either way for a yard.
The yard's merged geometry is 157,861 triangles across 8 meshes, up from ~75k, almost all of it the cobble field and the denser treeline.
